ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT) as amended; Executive Decree No. 129 of 25 June 2021 establishing the National Registry of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Registro de Beneficiario Final), administered by the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF); Law No. 9 of 1998 on Private Interest Foundations; Law No. 52 of 2016 on bearer shares; Resolution of the UAF on regulated subjects and customer due diligence. The Resident Agent is an obliged non-financial entity subject to UAF supervision and to ongoing CDD, UBO identification, record keeping (5 years) and STR reporting.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry of the founder's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the signatory's country duly legalized or Apostillized, or Panamanian Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each Founder, Council member, and Ultimate Beneficial Owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry/passport authority or Panamanian Notary upon verified copy of original

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory negative-media and sanctions screening of every Founder, Foundation Council member, Protector, and Beneficiary against the Panamanian UAF watchlists, OFAC SDN and Sectoral Sanctions lists, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU CFSP sanctions, and UK/domestic secondary sanctions lists, performed at onboarding and updated annually or upon any trigger event. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) applies to politically exposed persons, high-risk jurisdictions, and legal entities with opaque ownership. All screening evidence is archived in the AML file of the Resident Agent and retained for at least five years after termination of the professional relationship, per Law No. 23 of 2015 and UAF regulations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – 'Servicios en Línea' (https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa), Portal de Consultas de Nombres y Plataforma de Certificados de Disponibilidad de Nombre
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The chosen name may be in Spanish or any language written in Latin/Roman characters; usage of non-Latin scripts requires an official transliteration registered in the records. Names must be unique and not misleadingly similar to any existing Panamanian entity registered in the Public Registry. The name of a Private Interest Foundation must contain the term 'Fundación' or its recognized equivalent 'Foundation' in order to evidence the legal type, and may include the abbreviation 'Fund.' or 'PIF' as ancillary identifiers.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms suggesting a government, state, international organization or official sponsorship (e.g., 'Gobierno', 'Nación', 'National', 'United Nations', 'ONU', 'Cruz Roja', 'Red Cross')

Terms typical of licensed financial activities such as 'Banco', 'Bank', 'Seguros', 'Insurance', 'Reaseguros', 'Fiduciaria', 'Trust Company', 'Fondo de Inversión', 'Sociedad de Valores' where prior authorization of the Superintendency of Banks (SBP) or the Superintendency of Securities (SMV) is not exhibited
Terms implying a public-service or regulated professional activity (e.g., 'Hospital', 'Universidad' where no license exists)
Any name identical or phonetically/semantically confusingly similar to an existing registered Panamanian corporation, foundation, trust, trademark or trade name in the Registry database
Offensive, obscene or contrary-to-public-order terms, and any name attempting to evade the transparent identification of the foundation (e.g., 'Anónimo', 'Offshore' used alone)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On a negative name certificate, the applicant (through the Resident Agent) may re-apply with an alternative name without penalty. To contest a rejection, within five (5) business days of notification the applicant submits a written Recurso de Reconsideración addressed to the Director General del Registro Público de Panamá, citing the specific grounds of error in the similarity or prohibited-token assessment and attaching supporting evidence (e.g., trademark registration, authorization decree, or letters of consent from matching-name holders). If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant files a hierarchical Recurso de Apelación within five (5) business days for final administrative resolution by the higher registry authority; the alternate remedy is a timely re-filing under a modified name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A real Panamanian registered office with an actual physical address for service of process is mandatory and is ordinarily supplied by the licensed Resident Agent. Virtual-office arrangements are permitted only where the Resident Agent maintains permanent desk space and receives correspondence for the PIF; for this industry (CO2 laser-cut wooden puzzle design, assembly and e-commerce fulfillment through Amazon Pay and Stripe), no physical inventory or industrial facility is required in Panama, and the PIF may lawfully conduct its entire business from the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; statistically quantified at approximately 5% per annum for a non-regulated, low-risk private interest foundation carrying pure commercial e-commerce activity. The probability rises to approximately 15% where the foundation is flagged by adverse media, is connected to a PEP, or receives UAF/OFAC/UN enquiries, in which case the Public Registry or UAF may conduct unannounced verification of the registered office and ensure the documentation of the UBO file is physically available.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended by Law No. 13 of 2015; subsidiary application of the Panama Mercantile Code; key provisions include Article 19 (minimum initial endowment), Article 20 (registration of the foundation deed), Article 24 (mandatory registered office and resident agent), and Article 25 (foundation council and protector).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama) – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Private Interest Foundation Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (Public Deed of Incorporation of a Private Interest Foundation) executed before a Panama notary and registered in the Public Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: USD 10,000 minimum initial endowment (patrimonio inicial) subscribed by the founder and allocable in cash or in kind; no escrow account is mandated by law; the endowment must be fully subscribed at formation and the foundation deed must evidence its contribution, with the Public Registry tariff calculated on the declared endowment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned, being the initial Foundation Council of the Private Interest Foundation, hereby RESOLVE: (1) to accept the initial endowment of USD 10,000 subscribed by the founder; (2) to adopt as the registered office the premises located at [address], Panama, Republic of Panama; (3) to appoint [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Treasurer of the Foundation Council, each with full powers under the foundation charter; (4) to ratify the engagement of the resident agent law firm; (5) to open bank accounts and execute banking resolutions; and (6) to procure all industrial, municipal, environmental, and fire-safety clearances required for the wood puzzle manufacturing activity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of Panama in conjunction with a licensed Panama attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the foundation charter, founder identity documents, endowment subscription statement, and resident agent appointment letter to the notary. The notary drafts and reads the Escritura Pública de Constitución embodying the foundation name, purpose, endowment, registered office, Foundation Council, protector (if any), and registered agent; the founder and counsel execute the deed before the notary.
required_dossiers: Foundation charter (Reglamento)
Founder's passport copy and proof of legal capacity
Memorial or articles of incorporation draft
Power of attorney for the resident agent law firm
Bank reference letter or statement evidencing the USD 10,000 initial endowment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises an objection to the deed, the attorney must amend the instrument by clarifications or annexes and re-execute it before the same notary within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Public Deed with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the original certified notarial copy and two photocopies to the registry receiving window together with the registration request (solicitud de inscripción). Pay the official registration fee and registry tariff. The registry assigns a 'Ficha' record and issues the Certificate of Registry evidencing the foundation's juridical personality and legal existence.
required_dossiers: Original certified copy of the Public Deed
Photocopy of the resident agent's license and appointment
Registration request form signed by the attorney
Proof of payment of registry tariffs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry files a 'razón' or formal query, the filing attorney must cure the observation within 5 business days and resubmit the corrected photocopies; if the foundation name is rejected, the attorney must reserve an alternative name and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convene the first Foundation Council meeting and adopt resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foundation Council of the Private Interest Foundation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting at the registered office or by unanimous written consent; adopt the First Board Resolution approving the endowment, registered office, council officers, banking powers, and delegation to the resident agent; execute a certificate of meeting minutes and file it internally with the foundation records.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution draft
Foundation charter (Reglamento)
Acceptance letters of incoming council officers
Registered office acceptance letter from the resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any officer declines appointment, the Council may appoint a replacement by majority vote and amend the minutes or execute a supplementary resolution within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain municipal operating compliance and resident agent legalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía de Panamá (Municipal Mayor's Office) and the resident agent law firm
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación (municipal operating notice) with the Alcaldía, attaching the Certificate of Registry and foundation purpose description; the resident agent simultaneously files the annual franchise tax declaration and maintains the registered office. For the manufacturing activity, the municipal permit covers the commercial operation of the cutting and assembly workshop.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registry (Ficha)
First Board Resolution and officer identification
Municipal Aviso de Operación application form
Lease deed or registered office address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality requires additional zoning proof, submit a certified landlord letter and a description of the laser cutting activity to obtain the zoning clearance, then re-submit the Aviso within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the corporate bank account and payment rail arrangements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in Panama supervised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the registered deed, Certificate of Registry, First Board Resolution, and identity documents of officers and beneficiaries to the bank's compliance unit; complete the anti-money-laundering (AML) customer due diligence and sign the resolution authorizing Amazon Pay and Stripe settlement accounts for commercial receipts.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registry (Ficha)
Certified copy of the Public Deed and Council minutes
Passport copies and bank references of officers and founder
Bank account application and AML declaration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional source-of-funds evidence, submit three months of bank statements and a notarized declaration by the founder; re-submit the package within 10 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce and Industries (Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias – MICI), Industrial Policy and Authorizations Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Aviso de Operación for industrial manufacturing and commercial sale of wooden toys and educational puzzles; no separate national industrial patent is required for small-format laser fabrication

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación y Seguimiento Ambiental (Department of Environmental Assessment and Follow-up)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II – Environmental Registration (Registro Ambiental) applied to small-scale laser cutting and wood assembly workshops; full Environmental Impact Study (Estudio de Impacto Ambiental) is not required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Laser cutting equipment must incorporate particulate filtration (HEPA or equivalent) and exhaust treatment achieving stack outlet PM10 concentration below 50 mg/Nm³ and total VOC concentration below 100 mg/Nm³; no process wastewater discharge is permitted, and sanitary effluent must comply with the national maximum permissible discharge parameters (pH 6–9, BOD5 ≤ 220 mg/L, COD ≤ 400 mg/L) under COPANIT/ISO emission standards; wood waste, sawdust, and spent filters must be disposed of at an authorized solid waste facility and recorded in the MiAMBIENTE annual compliance report.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos (National Fire Department) fire-safety inspection certificate covering combustible wood dust, laser equipment thermal risk, and emergency egress; structural load inspection certificate issued by the Municipality verifying floor-load capacity for machinery; occupational health and safety program (Programa de Salud y Seguridad Ocupacional) filed with the Ministry of Labor (MITRADEL), including worker training records and industrial accident prevention measures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama; official e-services portal: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa and SICE electronic invoicing/clearance platform; customs counterpart for exporter registration and export declarations: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas de Panamá (ANA), portal https://www.ana.gob.pa (SIGA system).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) with non-resident founders/beneficiaries: (1) execute and register the foundation charter (escritura constitutiva) at the Registro Público de Panamá through a licensed resident agent, thereby creating the PIF as a Panamanian legal person; (2) obtain the certified digital signature (Firma Electrónica) from a DGI-accredited certification authority, required for all electronic tax filings and invoicing; (3) file the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) activation application on the DGI e-Tax portal, annexing the registered charter, bylaws, resident-agent acceptance, and identity documentation of the foundation council members, and declaring the ISIC 3240 activity (manufacture of games and toys) together with the exporter ITBMS regime; (4) DGI assigns the RUC/NIT tax identification number and, where the PIF is commercially active, adds ITBMS registration, authorizes electronic invoice series, and issues the taxpayer certificate; (5) a foreign entity without local incorporation but with Panamanian-source activity follows the same RUC route through a resident agent; (6) for physical exports, register with ANA as an exporter in the SIGA customs platform and link the exporter code to the RUC; (7) a purely passive PIF performing no Panamanian-source commercial activity is not required to register for RUC/ITBMS but must nonetheless satisfy the annual juridical annuity and legal fee requirements of Law 25 of 1995 to remain in good standing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope - Panama taxes only income derived from Panamanian sources. The PIF is exempt from income tax on its worldwide passive income and on assets held outside Panama, but a PIF carrying on manufacturing, assembly, or any commercial business within Panama is subject to entity-level corporate income tax at the standard rate of 25% on Panamanian-source profits (production/origin test); export sales of goods manufactured in Panama are also treated as Panamanian-source income under the territorial rule and remain taxable, while non-Panamanian passive income of the PIF stays outside the charge.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no US-style check-the-box election and no domestic hybrid-mismatch (BEPS Action 2) legislation. Available statutory elections and mechanisms: (i) the Foundation Council may elect to engage in commercial activities in Panama, voluntarily subjecting the PIF to the ordinary corporate tax and ITBMS regimes; alternatively, it may elect to keep the PIF as a passive exempt foundation; (ii) under Article 25 of Law 25 of 1995, a foundation that performs taxable acts in Panama is automatically taxed under the rules applicable to corporations; (iii) election as a small taxpayer (pequeño contribuyente) to apply the simplified ITBMS quota (cuota fija) regime where annual gross revenue does not exceed B/.200,000; (iv) no unilateral domestic election is available to invoke tax treaty benefits; treaty application, where any, is administrative and case-specific.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS - Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panama's value-added tax, a VAT/GST credit-method system on supplies of movable goods and services).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Panama does not impose a minimum turnover threshold for ITBMS registration; any person or entity that habitually or occasionally performs taxable transfers of movable goods or services in Panamanian territory must register in the RUC and charge ITBMS. Exporters must register regardless of turnover and may apply the 0% rate without any threshold. A simplified small-taxpayer regime applies to businesses with annual gross revenue not exceeding B/.200,000 (approximately US$200,000), allowing fixed-quota ITBMS payments instead of full periodic accounting.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing through the DGI SICE platform is mandatory, with phased roll-out to the entire RUC taxpayer base (major taxpayers from 2021-2022; all taxpayers by fiscal year 2025). The mandate requires real-time transmission of invoice data to DGI, DGI validation with an electronic seal and QR verification code before the invoice is legally effective, ERP/application-to-application integration via SICE APIs for high-volume issuers, digital certification (Firma Electrónica) for all issuers, and a distinct export-sales invoice category (tarifa 0%) that must reference the customs DUA. No paper invoicing remains for active commercial taxpayers; DGI automatically cross-matches invoicing, ITBMS returns, RUC status, and customs export records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating (tarifa 0%) applies to: (i) definitive exports of movable goods, including CO2 laser-cut wooden puzzle kits, that physically leave Panama under a customs DUA declared by the registered exporter; (ii) exported services performed in Panama but used exclusively abroad or benefiting non-residents outside Panama; and (iii) transfers of goods to duty-free zones and export-processing regimes (Colón Free Zone, Panamá Pacífico) where destined for re-export. The in-Panama assembly step does not disqualify zero-rating so long as the finished goods are exported within the permitted customs term and the export documents are in the exporter's name. To claim the 0% rate and the refund of input ITBMS credits, the PIF-exporter must hold a valid RUC/ITBMS registration, issue SICE-validated zero-rated export invoices, retain proof of physical departure, and evidence receipt of the foreign currency proceeds in a Panamanian bank account.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera - DUA) accepted and endorsed by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) in the SIGA system
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill / multimodal transport document) evidencing the shipment, consignee, and the port/gateway of exit
SICE/DGI-validated commercial e-invoice at tarifa 0% identifying the export transaction and referencing the DUA number
Packing list and the purchase order or sales contract underlying the export
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a Panamanian bank evidencing the export proceeds credited to the PIF's local account
SWIFT MT103 or bank credit confirmation proving receipt of payment from the foreign buyer
Certificate of Origin (where a preferential tariff treatment is claimed, including GSP and other trade agreements)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI and ANA verify zero-rating and refund claims by cross-matching DUA physical exit records, SICE e-invoice data, exporter bank statements, and upstream supplier invoices. A false or unsupported zero-rating claim triggers retrospective clawback of the full input ITBMS refunded, recapture of the standard 7% tax, the applicable statutory surcharge (recargo), monthly mora interest, and fines generally ranging from 50% to 300% of the credit fraudulently obtained. Additional consequences include removal from the DGI exporter refund list, suspension or cancellation of the RUC, and criminal prosecution for tax fraud under Panama Law 70 of 2019, carrying 5 to 10 years of imprisonment for intentional evasion or invoice falsification. The statutory prescription period for reassessment and clawback is three years, extended to five years in cases of fraud; foundation council members and the resident agent who sign export returns may incur joint liability for the penalties imposed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the banking regulator; Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent; monetary authority is effectively the U.S. Federal Reserve because Panama has no central bank and uses the U.S. dollar as legal tender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates under full de facto dollarization; the Balboa is a unit of account at fixed parity with the U.S. dollar. There are no capital controls, no exchange-control licensing, and no differentiated treatment between current and capital account transactions. Profit remittance, dividend distributions, royalty payments, and management fees are freely transferable abroad, subject only to bank-level AML/KYC due diligence and OFAC screening. Under Panama's territorial tax system, Panama-source income of a Private Interest Foundation is generally not subject to remittance blockage or non-resident withholding taxes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Exporters may freely hold, deposit, transfer, or reinvest U.S. dollar proceeds. Panamanian regulations do not impose a timeline for collecting or converting export proceeds; however, all export transactions must be reported to the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) for territorial tax assessment and to Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias for trade statistics.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium with legal constraints. Panama does not maintain a dedicated non-bank EMI license category equivalent to the EU's e-money institution framework; payment service providers must be authorized by the SBP or operate through licensed banks. Offshore digital EMIs cannot open direct multi-currency accounts for a Panamanian PIF unless they engage a licensed local correspondent bank. An offshore EMI may be used only as a payment gateway for Amazon Pay and Stripe settlement, with funds swept to a tier-1 local bank. The PIF must therefore maintain a physical banking anchor for capital escrow and trade disbursement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident Private Interest Foundation, most Panamanian tier-1 banks require at least one physical meeting with a foundation council member or an authorized legal representative. Remote opening is possible only where the bank accepts a notarized, apostilled power of attorney together with a live videoconference interview and certified ID documents. In practice, local private banks insist on physical presence of the resident agent or council member, while international branches such as Citibank may allow fully remote onboarding with enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foundation opacity: undeclared beneficial ownership due to the discretionary nature of the Private Interest Foundation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled foundation charter and by-laws; sworn declaration of beneficial owner and foundation council members; current registry excerpt from the Public Registry of Panama; SBP-compliant UBO identification form; notarized ID and proof of address of the beneficiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds mismatch for the initial capital injection from a foreign shareholder or founder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements or certified management accounts; signed capital contribution resolution; bank statements of the remitting entity documenting origin of funds; sale contracts with Amazon and Stripe for the laser-cut puzzle business; purchase invoices for CO2 laser machinery and wood raw material inventory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire transfer referencing a high-risk jurisdiction or an unexpected intermediary bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compliance screening results from OFAC, EU sanctions lists, and LexisNexis; chain-of-transaction narrative; commercial invoices aligned with ISIC 3240 scope; bill of lading or shipping airway bill; AML risk assessment showing Low_Risk_Standard; declaration of arms-length terms and economic substance of the PIF.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be sent via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign parent or shareholder to the PIF's tier-1 Panamanian account. The remitter should identify the purpose in SWIFT field 70 as 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'APORTE DE CAPITAL' and reference the foundation registration number. Panama does not use statutory government purpose codes, but banks require internal transaction reason codes and may request a predeposit letter, signed source-of-funds declaration, and proof of underlying commercial activity before accepting the wire. Transfers above USD 100,000 trigger automatic enhanced due-diligence review and may be escalated to the bank's compliance committee.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for raw material imports and logistics should clear through SWIFT MT103 for low-value payments, MT202 for bank-to-bank cover payments, and documentary letters of credit (MT700) for significant equipment purchases. For an LC, the PIF must present a commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, certificate of origin, and any required inspection certificate. The clearing bank will apply OFAC and anti-money-laundering filtering on all outbound wires; trade documents must demonstrate a genuine commercial nexus to the wooden puzzle manufacturing and assembly operations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forwards (USD/EUR and USD/CNH) entered into with licensed Panamanian banks or foreign subsidiaries
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on non-convertible or restricted currencies when physical delivery is impossible
FX swaps for temporary cross-currency liquidity bridging between USD and funding currencies such as EUR or CNH
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR and USD/CNH) for long-term equipment financing under an ISDA master agreement with an internationally licensed bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Flat Tax Payable (Tasa Única de Fundaciones)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) under the National Treasury; payment receipt available for Public Registry transactions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 December; a pro-rated first payment is due within 90 days after the foundation's incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs a monthly surcharge of 10% on the unpaid tax, capped at 100% of the tax; failure to pay for two consecutive years permits the Public Registry of Panama to administratively strike off and dissolve the foundation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation or Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Resident Agent and, through the agent, the Beneficial Ownership Registry maintained by DGI under Law 52 of 2016
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of the foundation charter; or within 30 days following any change in the founder, Foundation Council members, Protector, beneficiaries, or protective beneficial interests
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission, delay, or incorrect filing exposes the foundation and the Resident Agent to administrative fines from US$1,000 to US$10,000 per violation; there is no direct strike-off, but the Public Registry may suspend issuance of certifications while the UBO record remains non-compliant.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit applies to a passive Private Interest Foundation; a certified external audit becomes compulsory only if the foundation earns Panamanian-sourced annual gross income exceeding US$300,000, in which case audited financial statements must be filed with the DGI together with the income tax return.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted in Panama; small entities below audit thresholds may apply simplified local GAAP records, but a PIF is not required to publicly file financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The PIF has no share capital or members; beneficial ownership is evidenced by the foundation charter, by-laws, and any founding declaration or Protector's letter of wishes. The Resident Agent must maintain current UBO information under Law 52 of 2016. An annual confirmation of unchanged ownership is obtained at each anniversary date, and any amendment—including replacement of beneficiaries, Foundation Council members, or Protector—must be reported to the DGI beneficial ownership registry within 30 days. This protocol is a private confirmation held by the Resident Agent, not an open public filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries and Beneficial Interests (Registro de Beneficiarios)
Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions (Libro de Actas de la Fundación)
Inventory and Assets Register (Registro de Bienes y Activos)
Register of Foundation Council Members and Protector Appointments

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not normally required; if an IFRS audit is triggered, US$3,000 – US$8,000 per engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays apply to ISIC 3240 manufacturing. Panama's territorial tax system exempts foreign-source income, resulting in a 0% effective rate on offshore income and a 25% rate on Panama-source net income. Micro and small taxpayers may qualify for a simplified 2% gross receipts regime; standard depreciation for laser equipment remains available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 730 (Declaración Anual de Renta de Personas Jurídicas) / e-Tax Panama online portal (DGI)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before 31 March of the following fiscal year for calendar-year taxpayers; for non-calendar fiscal years, the last business day of the third month following fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: RUC, legal name, trade name, registered address, fiscal year-end, and foundation registry number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the PIF's Panamanian RUC and resident agent's local address. Foreign founder and beneficiary names are reported through the AML/beneficial ownership registry, not on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from Panamanian sources, including domestic sales of wooden puzzle kits, laser-cutting services, and related local income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not include foreign-source income. A PIF conducting no commercial activity in Panama reports zero in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating costs: cost of goods sold, wood and CO2 laser consumables, wages, equipment depreciation, rent, utilities, and shipping expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must be supported by invoices and accounting records maintained in Panama. Payments to non-resident related parties require transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after territorial adjustments, cost deductions, and utilization of prior-year loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the foundation is purely passive and holds foreign assets with no Panama-source income, enter zero and attach a statement explaining the foreign-source exclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable at the 25% statutory rate, prior to advance payments and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs with only foreign-source income owe zero. For any Panama-source commercial profit, compute 25% and pay in USD via the DGI system.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance income tax payments, customer withholdings, and other creditable tax prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Panamanian withholding certificates. Foreign tax credits are not permitted under the territorial system.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a surcharge of 10% of the tax due if filed within six months after the deadline; 20% if filed later. A monthly surcharge/interest of 2% accrues on the unpaid amount up to a maximum of 50%. Additional fines for failure to file range from US$50 to US$5,000 and the RUC may be suspended by the DGI.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% (standard dividend distribution withholding tax for Panamanian corporations; distributions from a Private Interest Foundation are generally not treated as dividends and no foundation-level dividend WHT arises)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must: (1) obtain a tax residence certificate (TRC) from its jurisdiction of residence; (2) obtain a Panamanian TRC when required; (3) submit a completed DGI treaty-relief form and the TRC to the paying entity before the payment date; and (4) retain documentation proving beneficial ownership and economic substance. Panama's DTA network is limited, and no treaty relief applies to distributions from a PIF unless expressly covered by an applicable convention.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 20% WHT to non-residents; treaty-reduced rates range from 5% to 10%. Interest: statutory 5% WHT to non-resident lenders; 0% applies to qualifying loans from foreign financial institutions; treaty rates generally cap at 5%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 2,000,000 (annual gross revenue or aggregate related-party transactions exceeding USD 2,000,000 trigger mandatory Transfer Pricing Informative Return and Local File / Master File preparation)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama Law 254 of 2021 (Economic Substance Regulations) applies to juridical persons, including Private Interest Foundations. Entities conducting relevant activities such as manufacturing must maintain a local registered office, adequate premises, local employees, and local management. A physical CO2 laser assembly facility for wooden puzzles satisfies ESR by operating production in Panama. Passive PIFs holding only foreign investments or IP must file the annual economic substance return and meet the reduced substance requirements for pure holding entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Panama-source revenues from the wooden puzzle manufacturing business, fabricating supplier invoices, or recording fictitious offshore expenses to reduce the 25% corporate income tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties of 2 to 5 times the evaded tax; imprisonment for 2 to 5 years; complete disallowance of fraudulent deductions; civil interest and late-payment surcharges of 10% to 50%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, administrators, and beneficial owners are jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax and penalties. Panama courts may issue travel bans, freeze personal assets, and impose commercial disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PIF as a mailbox entity with no laser assembly plant, no local employees, and no real management while processing Stripe/Amazon payments and offering Panamanian foundation status to foreign beneficiaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of the Economic Substance Regulations can trigger fines up to US$500,000 for serious infractions, automatic deregistration of the foundation, loss of tax-residency benefits, and suspension of the registered agent's license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Resident agents, directors, and administrators are personally liable for administrative penalties and third-party damages. The regulator may impose travel bans, strike the director from Panama's public registry, and order personal restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting funds through Amazon Pay and Stripe without implementing customer due diligence, failing to disclose the real beneficial owners, or funneling sales proceeds to third-party foreign accounts without any commercial justification under Law 23 of 2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of up to US$1,000,000 for non-compliant legal entities, freezing of bank accounts, administrative dissolution, and referral for criminal prosecution. Money laundering penalties include 5 to 10 years imprisonment and fines up to US$10,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers face personal criminal liability, civil restitution, travel bans, asset confiscation, and extradition risk. Non-resident founders lose the foundation's liability shield when they actively engage in laundering commercial proceeds.
